title: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church —  Old Testament 2026

items.text: Conversion is our goal. It is a process of change that influences our desires, our thoughts, our words, and our actions. As we come unto Christ and are born again, we can experience a profound and lasting transformation.
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: The Old Testament provides a foundation for understanding Jesus Christ and His gospel. It testifies of Him, His mission, and His Atonement. By studying its scriptures, we can deepen our faith and commitment to following Him.
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: The creation of the earth was a deliberate act of love by God. He organized it and filled it with life, establishing a pattern for us to follow. We are invited to be creators in our own lives, building and nurturing.

The Fall of Adam and Eve was a necessary step in God's plan, allowing for the progression of humanity. Though it brought sorrow, it also opened the door to eternal life through the Atonement of Jesus Christ.

Enoch taught the people to walk with God and to build a city where righteousness prevailed. Their faith and unity were so great that the Lord took Zion unto Himself. This demonstrates the power of living the gospel.

The covenant God made with Noah extended to all living creatures, a promise of preservation. This covenant reminds us of God's enduring love and His desire to bless His children, even amidst challenging times.

Abraham's faith and obedience were foundational to the covenant God made with him. He was promised an everlasting inheritance and that through his posterity, all nations would be blessed. This covenant continues to shape God's dealings with His children.

Sarah's faith was tested, yet she ultimately rejoiced in the promise of a child. Her experience teaches us about the importance of patience and trusting in God's timing, even when circumstances seem impossible.

Jacob's life was a testament to God's refining power. Through trials and repentance, he was transformed and renamed Israel, signifying a prince with God. His struggles and triumphs reveal the Lord's mercy and strength.

Joseph's story is a powerful example of forgiveness and divine providence. Despite betrayal and suffering, he rose to a position of influence and used it to save his family and many others, demonstrating God's ability to turn evil into good.
